title: Danny McBride’s ‘G.I. Joe’ Set for 2028 Release by Paramount, Announces The Hollywood Reporter
body:
Paramount Pictures has officially set an October 20, 2028 release date for its next “G.I. Joe” installment, confirming that the long‑awaited franchise revival will be helmed by comedian‑director Danny McBride. The studio also revealed that Academy‑award nominee Bradley Cooper will reprise the iconic role of Duke, the team’s charismatic leader, while McBride co‑writes the screenplay with veteran writer Jeff Fradley. The announcement, made on Friday, marks the firmest timeline yet for a project that has been shrouded in speculation for several years.

The decision to entrust the franchise to McBride signals a notable shift in tone for the action‑adventure series, which has historically leaned heavily on high‑octane combat and serious military drama. McBride, best known for his irreverent comedies such as “Eastbound & Down” and “The Ricky Gervais Show,” brings a distinct brand of humor that could inject fresh energy into the franchise’s formula. Industry insiders suggest that the script will blend the classic “G.I. Joe” ethos—teamwork, patriotism, and high‑tech warfare—with McBride’s signature off‑beat wit, potentially appealing to both longtime fans and a younger, comedy‑savvy audience.

Bradley Cooper’s involvement as Duke adds another layer of intrigue. While Cooper’s résumé is dominated by dramatic and thriller roles, his recent forays into action‑comedy—most notably the “Guardians of the Galaxy” series and the satirical “American Hustle”—demonstrate his versatility. Casting him as the stoic yet charismatic leader of the elite task force suggests Paramount is aiming for a performance that balances gravitas with a subtle, perhaps self‑aware, humor. Sources close to the production indicate that Cooper is collaborating closely with McBride to shape Duke’s character arc, ensuring the hero feels both familiar to veteran viewers and accessible to newcomers.

The announced release date places the film squarely in a competitive fall window, traditionally dominated by blockbuster franchises and awards‑season contenders. By targeting 2028, Paramount appears to be positioning “G.I. Joe” as a tentpole that can anchor its slate amid the growing dominance of streaming giants and the ongoing consolidation of theatrical releases. The extended lead time also allows the studio to fine‑tune visual effects, secure international distribution deals, and potentially align the movie with broader franchise plans, such as spin‑offs, television series, or cross‑media tie‑ins.

From a broader industry perspective, the revival of “G.I. Joe” reflects Hollywood’s continued reliance on established intellectual property to mitigate financial risk. The franchise, which originated as a 1960s toy line before expanding into comics, animated series, and live‑action films, still enjoys a robust global fan base. However, the market has become increasingly skeptical of formulaic sequels, prompting studios to reinvent legacy brands with fresh creative voices. McBride’s appointment is emblematic of this trend: a proven comedic auteur tasked with reimagining a classic action property for a new era.

Looking ahead, anticipation will build around how McBride’s comedic sensibilities integrate with the high‑stakes espionage world of “G.I. Joe.” Fans will be watching for early teasers, concept art, and casting announcements that could hint at the film’s visual style and narrative direction. If the partnership between McBride, Cooper, and Paramount succeeds in delivering a balanced blend of humor and heroism, the 2028 release could rejuvenate the franchise and set a precedent for how legacy action series evolve in the streaming age. The coming years will reveal whether this bold gamble pays off, but for now, the countdown to October 20, 2028, has officially begun.
